claims: I am Marcus Hale.
I play guitar in a band called Foxglove.
I teach guitar to kids out of my apartment in the Outer Sunset.
Foxglove has four members
My grandfather Walter gave me my first guitar when I was twelve.
The Gibson is from 1958 and it is the most valuable thing I own.
My youngest student is Aisha, who is nine.
Aisha has been learning from me for a year and already plays better than I did at her age.
The Chapel on Valencia Street holds four hundred people.
Selling it out is still our proudest achievement.
Lena is a nurse at the hospital on Parnassus and works long night shifts.
I live with my partner Lena in the Outer Sunset, two blocks from the beach.
Money is unpredictable as a musician.
I make most of my income teaching, and Foxglove barely covers the cost of touring.
Dev wants Foxglove to go on a national tour next year.
I am torn, because a long tour would mean leaving Lena and giving up my students for months.
My hearing has started to suffer from years of loud shows.
The doctor told me to wear earplugs on stage, and now I wear custom ones at every Foxglove gig.
Lena and I are saving to buy a small house outside the city.
Foxglove recorded our second album in a studio in Oakland over the winter.
Dev produced it himself, and we are releasing it at the Chapel in the spring.
I get terrible stage fright before big shows, even after six years.
I calm myself by tuning Walter's Gibson slowly in the dressing room before Foxglove goes on.
Lena worked through the whole pandemic at the hospital on Parnassus, and it changed her.
She tells me to chase the music while I still can.
One of my old students, now sixteen, just got into a music conservatory in New York.
The student is sixteen.
Dev and I argue about money more than anything else.
Lena talked me out of it the night before I was going to sign the offer.
The best part of my week is Saturday mornings, when Aisha comes for her lesson and plays me something new she figured out on her own.
